done_when: A review whose findings name files by an absolute path inside the checkout is kept, and those findings show the repo-relative path with no second review run.

known.title: Not done: Checkout paths cited through a symlink alias are discarded
Test: Checkout paths cited through a symlink alias are kept in one review

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - a macOS checkout under /var/folders is cited using that system alias.
The unmet item is: “A review whose findings name files by an absolute path inside the checkout is kept, and those findings show the repo-relative path with no second review run.” Git can report the worktree as /private/var/folders/... (the worktree path comes from src/forge/story.py:822-824), while /var/folders/... names the same files. Both checkout roots then use the /private spelling, so this prefix comparison misses the valid alias. Autoreview rejects the still-absolute path at tests/fixtures/autoreview-ce14dcca/scripts/autoreview:6811, discarding the report and triggering another review. Different valid casing on a case-insensitive macOS volume is also missed because the comparison folds case only on Windows.
findings.title: Not done: Checkout paths cited through a symlink alias are discarded

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - CI passes while a macOS review discards a finding that uses the /var checkout alias.
The tested item is: “A review whose findings name files by an absolute path inside the checkout is kept, and those findings show the repo-relative path with no second review run.” The test derives both spellings from the same worktree and never creates an alias. On the Linux pull-request runner with a non-symlink temporary directory, the raw and resolved spellings are identical, so both cases pass despite the current failure for a valid alias. The test also does not exercise a different valid spelling on a case-insensitive filesystem.
findings.title: Test: Checkout paths cited through a symlink alias are kept in one review

why: A review finding that names a file by its absolute path makes the review helper discard the whole review, so its tokens (about 3M once) are wasted and the review runs again.
